question: What technologies were used to build the Quizzy platform, and what core functionalities did it provide?
expected_answer: Quizzy is a distributed quiz management platform built using Java, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Spring Data JPA, Spring Data MongoDB, Netflix Eureka, OpenFeign, JWT, MongoDB, SQL, REST APIs, and Maven. The platform provided RESTful APIs to create, launch, update, and play quizzes, as well as manage quiz attempts and enforce scheduling and attempt limits. MongoDB was used for quiz data storage, while Spring Data JPA handled relational data management. JWT-based authentication was implemented for security, Netflix Eureka handled service discovery, and OpenFeign enabled inter-service communication. The project ran from June 2026 to July 2026.

question: Describe the MiPA (My Personal Assistant) project — its architecture, key technologies, and core features.
expected_answer: MiPA is an AI-powered personal assistant developed using LangChain and LangGraph, featuring autonomous tool orchestration and personalized assistance. It leverages the Model Context Protocol (MCP) through dedicated, cloud-deployable MCP servers built for tool execution and long-term memory management. The backend uses FastAPI with JWT-secured REST APIs. For data persistence, MongoDB Atlas is used for persistent memory and Supabase (PostgreSQL) for application data, with SQLAlchemy as the ORM. MiPA's core capabilities include event scheduling, personal finance tracking and analysis, web search, knowledge retrieval, and a Self-RAG-based document question-answering system. The full technology stack includes Python, FastAPI, LangChain, LangGraph, MCP, MongoDB Atlas, Supabase, SQLAlchemy, JWT, and Self-RAG. It was developed between May 2026 and August 2026.

question: What is HisNet, what model architecture does it use, and what classification accuracy did it achieve?
expected_answer: HisNet is a Vision Transformer-Based Osteosarcoma Detection system developed between October 2025 and March 2026. It uses a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder-only model built with TensorFlow and Keras for detecting osteosarcoma from histopathological Whole Slide Images (WSIs). The model was trained and evaluated on datasets from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), with image augmentation applied to improve generalization. HisNet achieved 86.9% classification accuracy while maintaining a compact model size of 28 MB, including optimizer parameters, with ongoing work focused on further improving model performance.
